record.program_name: County surplus land inventory and exempt surplus declarations (Surplus Land Act)
record.administering_agency: Mendocino County Executive Office (Darcie Antle, CEO; Steve Dunnicliff)
record.typical_award_size: On December 16, 2025 the Board approved the annual Surplus Land Act inventory and five resolutions declaring parcels surplus or exempt surplus: the Covelo Community Services District office (23950 Grange Street, Covelo; redeclared exempt surplus January 20, 2026), the Boonville Veterans Memorial Building (14470 Highway 128), an Anchor Bay parcel, 120 W. Fir Street and a small vacant parcel. The inventory is published in the Housing Element APR (Table H) as the County's list of land available to housing developers.
record.affordability_requirement: Surplus Land Act: 25% lower income units for 55 years if a housing developer acquires non-exempt surplus land.
record.next_deadline: Watch HCD's surplus land notices and the County's annual December inventory; most 2025 parcels are small civic buildings rather than housing sites.
record.layering_notes: Mendocino County has no housing department: the Executive Office Grants Division administers state CDBG and HOME program income, Social Services is the administrative entity for the Mendocino County Homeless Services Continuum of Care (CA-509) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, NPLH and bridge housing, Planning and Building Services handles density bonus and the Housing Element, and the Community Development Commission of Mendocino County (CDC, the housing authority) supplies vouchers and owns housing. The County repealed its inclusionary ordinance on September 10, 2024, has no housing trust fund money, no NOFA and no impact fee waiver; County capital help has come from state pass-through grants (CDBG-DR, Homekey) and small HOME program income balances. Ukiah and Fort Bragg run their own programs (Pass 3). mendocinocounty.gov, the Legistar web API client 'mendocino', mendocino.granicusideas.com and cdchousing.org all open normally. Recorded because the HHAP-6 regional plan points developers to the APR Table H list; no County land has been offered for affordable housing in 2025-2026. Source is the December 16, 2025 Board item (Legistar web API matter 14211).
eligible_project_detail: small rural sites for affordable or farmworker housing

record.program_name: Fort Bragg Inclusionary Housing Requirements and Inclusionary Housing Trust Fund (Coastal LUDC Chapter 17.32 and Inland LUDC Chapter 18.32; Ordinance 1029-2026)
record.administering_agency: City of Fort Bragg Community Development Department
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Non-subdivision projects of 5 to 10 units (rental or for-sale) must make 20% of units affordable by design; for-sale projects of 11 to 20 units 10% inclusionary and 21 or more units 15%; rental projects over 10 units owe inclusionary units only when they request a density bonus or incentive. Alternatives: land donation, small secondary units (two per inclusionary unit in 11 to 30 lot subdivisions), in-lieu fee set by Council resolution. In-lieu fees and resale equity recapture go to the Inclusionary Housing Trust Fund (17.32.090), restricted to affordable housing acquisition, construction and reimbursement of excess affordable units. Fund balance not published.
record.affordability_requirement: Rental inclusionary units: half at 80% AMI and half at 120% AMI, with priority for essential public service employees; rental affordability term 25 years. For-sale units: 15-year resale control with equity sharing back to the Housing Trust Fund. Affordable projects restricted at least 15 years are exempt.
record.next_deadline: Ordinance 1029-2026 (coastal zone amendments to 17.31 and 17.32) passed in September 2026 and takes effect upon California Coastal Commission certification; verify certification date with the City.
record.layering_notes: A 2023 City Attorney memo notes Fort Bragg's 20% requirement for 5 to 10 unit projects and no requirement for larger rental buildings without a bonus. A November 12, 2024 hearing on an inclusionary in-lieu fee resolution and nexus study is referenced in a City notice, but city.fortbragg.com returned 502 errors and timeouts this pass, so the adopted fee amount was not confirmed. Trust fund money could serve as local gap funding for tax credit projects but no NOFA or award process was found. The County repealed its inclusionary ordinance; Fort Bragg runs its own. Ordinance read from the City's Legistar attachment host (Legistar web API client 'cityfortbragg').
